facts.heading: Anxiety is constant
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time. This anxiety got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Work change in September
facts.content: Hannah's deputy head left, and she was asked to step up.
facts.evidence: when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of incompetence
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety manifests physically
facts.content: Hannah experiences physical symptoms when thoughts arrive.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential criticism
facts.content: Hannah rehearses possible questions and how she will be perceived.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say, then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines others thinking she is incapable.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Fear of being perceived as stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Lying about capability
facts.content: Hannah feels she is pretending to be capable.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feeling like a child
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a headteacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for twenty years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy
facts.content: Hannah's mother was brilliant and is remembered positively in the village.
facts.evidence: She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Comparing her work
facts.content: Hannah compares her current job to her mother's career.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Minimizing distress
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad things are.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss, so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at 4 AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 every morning. She falls asleep fine. She spends time going through her to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at 4 every morning. I fall asleep fine. Then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking due to tasks
facts.content: Hannah has many things on her to-do list. These include timetable changes, offset prep, a parent complaint, and a worried child.
facts.evidence: Everything. Timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about. It goes round and round.

facts.heading: Increased coffee consumption
facts.content: Hannah drinks a lot of coffee to get through the day. She knows this does not help her.
facts.evidence: I drink a lot of coffee to get through a day which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Drinking five or six coffees
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee. This prevents her from sitting still in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: Five or six, then I can't sit still in the afternoons.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences physical symptoms during the afternoons. Her heart goes fast and her hands are shaky.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water. She did not think anyone noticed.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday, I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted daily
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day because of pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben knows a bit about how she is feeling. He suggested she should just enjoy it.
facts.evidence: My partner Ben knows a bit. He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Guilt and loneliness
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben gives that advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone. He means well.

facts.heading: Partner's profession
facts.content: Ben is an engineer. He believes that if something is a problem, it can be fixed.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.

facts.heading: Wish for simplicity
facts.content: Hannah wishes the situation were simpler.
facts.evidence: No, I wish it were that simple.

facts.heading: Loss of social connections
facts.content: Hannah no longer has friends at school. She used to eat lunch with others but is now their line manager.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year for a quarter with the others. Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Missing former peers
facts.content: Hannah misses her former classmates and her class.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Desire for promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion. She said yes because she could not say no to her.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Crying after promotion
facts.content: Hannah went home and cried after accepting the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Fear about the future
facts.content: Hannah felt fear and worry about the future regarding the promotion.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Lack of validation
facts.content: People only say 'well done' instead of asking how she feels.
facts.evidence: Nobody has asked me that, they just say well done.

facts.heading: Time of relaxation
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Relaxation environment
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of her. She was just walking while Ben carried the sandwiches.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking. Ben carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Return to stress
facts.content: The week before term, Hannah was a wreck again. She could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. She stopped after two weeks because she felt silly.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a true laughing, a good email. It held for about two weeks, and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Feeling like a fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do her job without feeling like a fraud. This would look like not rehearsing in meetings and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling lighter after goals
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter and a bit tearful when stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful actually.

facts.heading: Telling someone about 4am
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad her 4am experiences are. Ben does not know about this.
facts.evidence: It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah finds telling Ben scary because he would probably be hurt that she did not say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Plan to tell Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben this week. She needs a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening.
facts.evidence: I might try this week. If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening.

facts.heading: When to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah plans to tell Ben over breakfast on Saturday morning. Ben is always in a good mood then.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast. He is always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Reattempting evening writing
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for a week. She will put it by the kettle to avoid forgetting.
facts.evidence: I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.content: Hannah nearly cancelled an appointment this morning. She is glad she did not cancel.
facts.evidence: lady I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
